SQL steps: reading a step's rows, RETURNING, how params bind, the tenant key in flow SQL, `expect_rows` and `rows_affected`, and numbers written as text.

INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE must use `RETURNING <col>` for `steps.<id>.outputs.<col>` to resolve downstream - without it the ref halts the flow with `template_unresolved`. Use `| default:''` for genuinely-optional refs.

Row access on a step's result set: `steps.<id>.outputs.<col>` (first row's column, single-row sugar), `steps.<id>.outputs.rows[0].<col>` (explicit index), and `steps.<id>.outputs.first.<col>` (alias for row 0) ALL resolve to the same value - for SELECT and INSERT…RETURNING alike. `steps.<id>.outputs.rows` is the whole slice. NOTE: any row ref is only valid when the step returned ≥1 row - guard a 'has rows' branch with `if: ${{ steps.<id>.outputs.rows }}` (empty result → falsy) and reference the row INSIDE it, or the ref halts template_unresolved on an empty result.

**Group scoping is NOT auto-injected into flow SQL.** Auto-CRUD POST sets the org/group key for you; a flow's `run: sql` INSERT does NOT - omit it and the row lands with a NULL group key, invisible to every org-scoped read (looks like a silent data-loss bug). Set it EXPLICITLY: `INSERT INTO t (..., org_id) VALUES (..., ${{ user.group_id }})` (`${{ user.group_id }}`/`${{ user.org_id }}` resolve to the caller's group), or POST through the auto-CRUD endpoint instead of a flow. A signed-in caller who belongs to no tenant has no `user.group_id`, and a step that references it bare fails with a 500 for that caller. Bind `${{ user.group_id || 0 }}` in the step that checks the caller's membership (it then finds no row) and answer 403 before any INSERT; api({at:'tasks'}) `multi_tenant` shows the flow.

**Numeric-looking params bind as NUMBERS.** A `:param` whose value round-trips canonically ('5000', '6.5') binds as int64/float64, so guards like `WHERE :amt >= (SELECT SUM(...))` compare NUMERICALLY (SQLite ranks TEXT above ANY number when neither side has column affinity, so as text '5000' >= 10515 would be true). Non-canonical strings ('01234', '5e3', '+1') bind as TEXT, so zip codes / phone numbers keep exact equality. No `CAST(:param AS REAL)` is needed.

**Guarded writes: assert with `expect_rows`, don't trust a 200.** The classic trap is `INSERT INTO t SELECT ... WHERE <guard>`: when the guard is false, 0 rows insert but the flow STILL returns 200 {ok} - the write silently did nothing. Add `expect_rows: ">0"` (also `>=1`, `=1`, `!=0`, `<=N`, or a bare number meaning `=N`) to the step so the flow FAILS LOUD when the guard blocked the write, instead of reporting success. Prefer this over re-deriving `changes()` by hand. A write without `RETURNING` also stores its count as the step output `rows_affected`: read it as `${{ steps.<id>.outputs.rows_affected }}` to branch or report (`if: ${{ steps.mark.outputs.rows_affected }} == 0`). Any other output column whose name starts with `rows` (`rows_written`, `rows_total`) is read the same way.

**`expect_rows` is checked on every `run: sql` / `run: sql_dynamic` statement.** It compares the rows RETURNED by a `SELECT` / `WITH ... SELECT` and by an `INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ... RETURNING` (one row per row changed), and the rows AFFECTED by any other `INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE`. So `expect_rows: "=1"` on a lookup means 'exactly one row exists', and on `UPDATE ... RETURNING id` 'exactly one row changed'. A `WITH ... INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` without RETURNING also stores `{rows_affected: n}` as its output, like any other write. A failed assertion is a step error: the caller gets a 500 and the server log says `sql: expect_rows assertion failed on step "<id>": N row(s) returned|affected, expected <expr>`. It undoes what the flow already wrote only when `on.request` has `transaction: true`; without it earlier steps, and a write that changed the wrong number of rows, stay applied (the log line says which).

**Where `expect_rows` goes.** Write it at the step root, next to `run:` - that is the canonical position. Under `with:`, next to `params`, it is read as the same assertion, and the two positions must not disagree. Always quote a comparison (`expect_rows: "!=0"`): unquoted, YAML reads `!=0` as an empty value; a bare integer (`expect_rows: 1`) is fine. The write gate and `benmore check` refuse an `expect_rows` that could not be checked: on a step that is not SQL (api, set, an `if:` block, a `for_each:` loop - put it on the query that feeds the loop; a `with:` key of `run: set` is a variable and may have any name), with no value, written in both positions with different values, or on a statement with no row count - DDL, PRAGMA, or a step of several statements unless every one is an INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE without RETURNING (then the last one is counted). At run time a SQL step whose assertion cannot be checked refuses to run; it never runs unchecked.

**A number computed in SQL and written as text keeps the digits it has (SQLite 3.53).** `json_object('total', price * qty)`, `json_array(..)`, `CAST(x AS TEXT)`, `x || ''` and `printf('%s', x)` write a REAL with 15 significant digits when that reads back as the same number and with 17 when it does not: `4.35 * 100` is `434.99999999999994`, `0.1 + 0.2` is `0.30000000000000004`, and `SUM()` / `AVG()` over REAL prices can end the same way (19.99 + 5.01 + 0.1 is `25.099999999999998`). It is the value the same number always had when it reached JSON as a number column. Round where you compute: `json_object('total', round(SUM(price * qty), 2))`, or `printf('%.2f', ..)` for text. A value stored as it was entered (19.99), `round()` results and INTEGER arithmetic (cents) are written as they are.

A SQL step may create, alter and drop the app's own tables (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS my_cache ...`), but not the framework's: CREATE, DROP or ALTER of a `_benmore_*` table, index, trigger or view, an index or trigger on a `_benmore_*` table, and `PRAGMA writable_schema` fail the step with `app SQL may not ...`. Reading and writing rows of framework tables is unchanged. See api({at:'schema'}) -> framework_tables.
